summary: PulseGuard v0.6.38 completes the updater/architecture work from v0.6.37 by extracting the maintenance and recovery subsystem from the monolithic UI script into a dedicated, self-healing runtime engine without changing its public function contracts or repair policy.

sections.heading: Maintenance/recovery engine is external again
sections.detail: The Get/Invoke-PGM maintenance, Windows Update, component-store, filesystem, DNS, VSS, activation, recovery-readiness, storage-optimization and source-coverage functions now live in Runtime\PulseGuard_MaintenanceEngine.ps1 instead of being inlined into Our_PC_Optimizer.ps1. Existing function names and callers are unchanged.

sections.heading: Extraction remains compatible with existing updater generations
sections.detail: The v0.6.37 shape-based updater accepts the dedicated PulseGuard_*Engine.ps1 module, while the prior v0.6.36 exact allowlist already included PulseGuard_MaintenanceEngine.ps1 and its Recovery counterpart.

sections.heading: The engine participates in runtime self-heal
sections.detail: PulseGuard now ships a Recovery copy of the maintenance engine, restores the runtime copy if it is genuinely missing, verifies both copies in the supported runtime layout, and removes obsolete root-level copies during migration cleanup.

sections.heading: Release validation now requires the extracted engine
sections.detail: The v0.6.38 updater treats both Runtime\PulseGuard_MaintenanceEngine.ps1 and its Recovery copy as required payload files, preventing a future release from staging an incomplete maintenance subsystem.

sections.heading: v0.6.37 correctness and rollback fixes remain included
sections.detail: The GIGABYTE detection, ownership-path, compatibility-layer, grid sorting, startup-entry isolation, Privacy Sweep, rollback batching, updater allowlist and targeted exception-logging fixes from v0.6.37 remain in this build.
